data.description: A 57-year-old female without any medical history was admitted for evaluation of a left ventricular tumor that was discovered incidentally. The patient was asymptomatic and had no relevant past medical history. Physical examination findings were not specifically described in the case report.

A rare benign vascular tumor of the heart composed of proliferating blood-filled vascular channels. It may arise in the ventricular myocardium and often shows progressive contrast enhancement on cardiac MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging appearance of a well-defined vascular-appearing lesion with progressive enhancement
Histology showing vascular channels within fibrous stroma

data.description: A benign tumor composed predominantly of fibroblasts and dense collagen, usually arising within the ventricular myocardium. It is more common in children but can rarely occur in adults.
symptoms_in_common: Fibrous tissue visible on histologic staining
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive vascular-type contrast enhancement typical of a hemangioma
Grossly yellow-tan soft appearance rather than a firm fibrous mass

data.description: The most common primary benign cardiac tumor, usually arising in the left atrium from the interatrial septum. Ventricular myxomas are uncommon and may cause obstruction or embolization.
symptoms_in_common: Female patient in the typical adult age range
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular myocardial location rather than the usual left atrial septal location
Vascular-channel histology rather than myxoid stroma with stellate cells
Progressive enhancement pattern suggestive of a vascular tumor

data.description: A malignant endothelial-cell tumor of the heart that most often arises in the right atrium and may invade surrounding structures or metastasize. It can have hemorrhagic and highly vascular imaging features.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac mass with vascular characteristics on imaging
Can occasionally be detected before symptoms develop
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular location; angiosarcoma usually involves the right atrium
No constitutional symptoms, pericardial effusion, or signs of invasive disease
Histology without reported malignant cellular atypia, necrosis, or infiltrative growth
